decision_note: Moreira et al. 2019 is a meta-analysis of herbivore effects on floral traits, pollinator attractiveness and reproductive success. It remains synthesis/source-registry evidence but is not double-counted as a primary included study.
Aygoren Uluer 2021 is explicitly a review article on papilionaceous-flower pollinators; retain bibliographically but exclude from the primary-study count.
Barman et al. 2023 is explicitly a review of cucurbit floral scents, pigments, pollinators and florivores; useful source-registry material, not a primary included experiment.

claim_ceiling: Primary thesis experiment recovers herbivory effects on floral display and pollinator foraging with female fitness measured, but the display A axis itself is not manipulated and antagonist response to A is absent
decision_note: Lythrum salicaria herbivory treatments changed display architecture and pollinator foraging; no detectable fruit/seed-production difference. Near-pass only because herbivory, not A, is manipulated.
bioRxiv preprint of the dataset published as SCHPRISMA-000036 / New Phytologist 10.1111/nph.16739; exclude duplicate report and retain the version of record.

claim_ceiling: Direct evidence that pleiotropy/genetic linkage can correlate floral and herbivory-induced volatile evolution; no pollinator/antagonist response coefficients or net fitness surface
decision_note: Xu et al. 2020 links allelic variation at clustered terpene synthases to correlated floral and herbivory-induced volatile variation. Evolutionary architecture evidence only; consumer responses are not the focal experiment.

claim_ceiling: Soil amendment increased growth, flower number, visitors and seed yield and altered herbivore performance, but the focal floral A coordinate is not randomized independently
decision_note: Barragan-Fonseca et al. 2023 measures pollinator attraction, herbivore performance and seed yield under a common upstream soil treatment. Near-pass/context evidence, not a strict do(A) experiment.

claim_ceiling: Strong same-code behavioral near-pass: floral scent/linalool directly manipulated and adult feeding versus female oviposition measured, but no common plant reproductive outcome
decision_note: Reisenman et al. 2010 shows enantiomer-specific antagonism between Manduca feeding and oviposition pathways on the same Datura floral scent coordinate. It does not close the strict fitness gate.

claim_ceiling: Aphid infestation causally changes floral chemistry and pollinator attractiveness, especially in females; it does not measure antagonist response to manipulated A or a common plant-fitness outcome
decision_note: Zill et al. version of record (J Exp Bot, eraf522). Retain published article; duplicate bioRxiv report SCHPRISMA-000052 is excluded.
bioRxiv preprint of the study published as SCHPRISMA-000051 / Journal of Experimental Botany 10.1093/jxb/eraf522; exclude duplicate report.

claim_ceiling: Nectar supplementation directly increases oviposition by a moth that is also a pollinator, but the focal experiment does not measure the pollinator response to nectar or a common reproductive outcome
decision_note: Adler & Bronstein 2004 experimentally supplements Datura nectar and recovers increased Manduca oviposition. Pollinator function is system natural history rather than a same-study response coefficient.

Lophophytum brood-pollination study directly documents adult pollinators and larvae developing in reproductive tissues but does not define or test a focal floral attraction/display coordinate A. Derived brood pollination is a historical hypothesis, not a cue-transition test.

claim_ceiling: Direct anti-herbivore function of an inflorescence display previously shown to attract pollinators; same-study pollinator response and common fitness are absent
decision_note: Gerchman et al. 2012 tests herbivore discrimination/feeding on Salvia viridis purple flags. Retain as display-function near-pass, not a same-study linked pollinator-antagonist experiment.
